agencies.decision_summary: Board of Commissioners voted 4-0 at a Sept 8 special meeting (one member absent) to cancel the Sheriff's Office $219,000 Flock stationary-ALPR contract outright, rejecting a pause option. Cited privacy, vendor policy shifts, and misuse cases (including a former Brunswick County SO employee). System had been searched ~3 million times since Jan 2025. County manager to work out cancellation with the sheriff; refund request for unused term.
agencies.notes: Board of Commissioners voted 4-0 at a Sept 8 special meeting to cancel the Sheriff's Office Flock stationary-ALPR contract outright, rejecting a pause. The contract was reported at $219,000, but the sources do not confirm that figure is an annual amount, so cost is null. Cited privacy, vendor policy shifts, and misuse cases (including a former Brunswick County SO employee). System had been searched ~3 million times since Jan 2025. Refund requested for unused term. State-funded cameras unaffected.

sources.title: Wrightsville Beach police officer out after alleged Flock misuse
Former Wrightsville Beach officer charged with misuse of Flock cameras

agencies.notes: County budget funds 32 LPRs (29 fixed, 1 pending install, 4 offline from damage, plus 3 portable). Sheriff Hobart Lewis told the county Public Safety Committee each camera costs $3,500/yr plus $900 one-time install; county sets 30-day retention and says it does not sell data. Two deputies were fired in July 2026 for Flock misuse; sheriff addressed committee Aug 10. Agency remains active. SC DPS separately said it is 'in the process of potentially renewing' its HQ Flock contract (Greenville Business Magazine, Sept 2026) - worth watching for a renewal date but no agency-specific terms published.

sources.title: Greenville County sheriff addresses Flock camera concerns after deputies fired

agencies.notes: Contract remains ACTIVE; no cancellation. On Sept 9, 2026 the department announced it had fired and charged 3 officers: Renee Downer (arrested May, simple battery + stalking), Derric Holmes (6 counts misuse of license plate data), Matthew Lau (1 count). A new June audit system exposed the abuse. Reforms: supervisor approval + written justification per search, mandatory retraining, retention cut from 30 to 15 days. Gwinnett County PD is the 3rd-highest searcher of Lexington KY's Flock system per WKYT. Town hall with residents planned/follow-up per WSB-TV.
